header.title: Player guide
header.intro: Gachapon blends two game loops: <collect>collecting</collect> cards by pulling capsules, and <battle>battling</battle> with them in the campaign to progress. Here's everything you need to get started and play smart.

monnaies.intro: Five resources drive the game. Your balance of each is shown live in the topbar.

gachaTokens.name: Gacha tokens
gachaTokens.description: The currency for pulls. Every capsule costs one token. They regenerate on their own up to a cap.

dust.name: Dust
dust.description: Earned from duplicates. Used in the daily shop, for wishes, to level up your cards, and to reset your skill tree.

gold.name: Gold
gold.description: Earned in battle and from quests. Mainly used to raise the level of your cards.

combatPoints.name: Combat points
combatPoints.description: The campaign's energy. Regenerates over time up to a cap; every battle or farm run uses some.

xp.name: XP & level
xp.description: Earned by pulling and battling. Leveling up unlocks skill points and milestone rewards.

skillPoints.name: Skill points
skillPoints.description: Earned by leveling up. Invest them in the skill tree for permanent passive bonuses.

tokens.intro: Gacha tokens are the game's action currency — every capsule pull uses one. They regenerate automatically over time, with nothing to do on your end.
tokens.capBullet: Your token stock has a cap: tokens earned beyond it are lost. Come back regularly.
tokens.regenBullet: Regeneration is continuous: your balance is recalculated on the fly every time you log in.
tokens.topbarBullet: The topbar shows your balance and the time until your next token.
tokens.info: You can also get tokens from the Shop (token packs) or events. Some skills speed up regeneration, raise the cap, or give a chance at a bonus token.
tokens.tip: Tip: log in regularly to avoid hitting the cap and losing accumulated tokens.

pulls.intro: A pull uses 1 token and gives you a random card from the active pool. Every card has a drop weight: the higher the weight, the more likely the card.
pulls.instantBullet: The pull is instant — the result shows up live over WebSocket.
pulls.resultBullet: The result includes the card, its variant, whether it's a duplicate, and the dust earned.
pulls.pityBullet: Your pity counter updates after every pull (see the dedicated section).
pulls.skillsParagraph: Several skills affect pulls: they boost the odds of <rareBadge></rareBadge> <epicBadge></epicBadge> <legendaryBadge></legendaryBadge> rarities, buff variant odds, give a chance at a <freePull>free pull</freePull>, or trigger a <goldenBall>golden ball</goldenBall> that forces a minimum rarity.

rarete.intro: Every card belongs to one of five rarities, from most common to rarest:
rarete.variantIntro: Cards of <strong1>RARE, EPIC, and LEGENDARY</strong1> rarity can appear in a special version called a <strong2>variant</strong2>:

normal.name: NORMAL
normal.description: The card's standard version, the most common one.

brilliant.name: BRILLIANT
brilliant.description: The brilliant version — generates more dust as a duplicate.

holographic.name: HOLOGRAPHIC
holographic.description: The holographic version — the rarest variant, generates even more dust.

rarete.ratesOutro: Variant odds depend on rarity: a Legendary is more likely to be Holographic than a Rare. Exact rates are configured by the admins.

piete.intro: The pity system guarantees that no player can pull forever without getting a Legendary card. A counter increases with every pull that isn't a Legendary.
piete.thresholdBullet: When the counter reaches the threshold, the next pull is guaranteed Legendary.
piete.resetBullet: Getting a Legendary — before the threshold or thanks to pity — resets the counter to zero.
piete.personalBullet: Pity is personal: it isn't shared, and it persists across sessions.
piete.info: Your pity counter is visible on your profile. A dedicated skill lets you lower the threshold to hit Legendaries more often.
